_note: Phone numbers must be re-confirmed with NCDA / RIB before the evaluation sessions.

items.title: Use the right names for body parts
items.body: Children who know the correct words can explain what happened. Name private parts calmly, the same way you name an elbow or a knee.

items.title: Surprises, not secrets
items.body: Explain the difference: a surprise is fun and is told soon (a birthday gift). A secret that makes you feel worried should always be told.

items.title: Practise a strong NO together
items.body: In the lessons your child practises saying NO out loud: loud, low and short, like "NO." not "no?". Practise at home too, and say no to games yourself sometimes. Praise the voice, and show that NO is respected, even when it is said to you.

items.title: Ask after each lesson
items.body: Ask your child to teach you STOP. Let them name their trusted adults, and add yourself to the list if you are not there yet.

items.title: If your child tells you something
items.body: Stay calm, believe them, thank them for telling you, and tell them it is not their fault. Do not question them in detail; contact the services below.

items.title: Changes in behaviour
items.body: Sudden fear of a person or place, withdrawal, anger, bed-wetting or nightmares that were not there before.

items.title: Secrets and gifts
items.body: New gifts, money or phone credit from an adult, with no clear reason, or talk of a special secret.

items.title: Knowledge beyond their age
items.body: Words or play about adult sexual behaviour that a child of their age would not usually know.

items.title: Physical signs
items.body: Pain, bruising or bleeding around private areas, or difficulty walking or sitting. Seek medical help at an Isange One Stop Centre.

items.title: Child Helpline (free)
items.body: National toll-free line for children and anyone worried about a child.

items.title: Isange One Stop Centre
items.body: Free medical, psychosocial and legal help for child abuse and GBV, in hospitals across Rwanda.

items.title: Emergency (Rwanda National Police)
items.body: If a child is in danger right now.

items.title: Your village IZU volunteer
items.body: Inshuti z'Umuryango volunteers in every village can help families find support.
